title: Data with the Stars: 421 Entries, Two Scoring Systems, One Bobby Bones
dek: A math-modeling contest asked students to separate judge scores from secret fan votes on Dancing with the Stars. The public data shows why nobody can read the answer off the scoreboard.

blocks.text:
Dancing with the Stars is the American version of the British format Strictly Come Dancing, originally Come Dancing. Each week celebrities dance with professionals, a judges' panel scores the dance, and viewers vote for the couple they want to keep. The two numbers are combined, and the lowest combined score goes home.

Viewers can vote to keep a star but cannot vote to send one home. COMAP notes that judge scores are meant to reflect technique, while fan votes are likely swayed by popularity and charisma as well.
Two ways to add up a dance

COMAP's problem statement says seasons 1 and 2 combined judge scores and fan votes by rank. After season 2, when Jerry Rice reached the final despite very low judge scores, the show moved to percentages.

In season 27 Bobby Bones won despite consistently low judge scores. From season 28 the bottom two were found from the combined score and the judges then chose who left. COMAP says the show also seems to have gone back to ranks around then, and that the exact season is not known, so season 28 is an assumption.

We took each contestant's average judge score: the mean, across the weeks they were scored, of that week's average per judge. On that rough measure the four contestants COMAP names as controversial finished well above where the judges would have put them.

This is a quick calculation, not the contest's method. Judges, dances and score scales change from week to week, so treat the ranks as a sketch. [VERIFY: re-run in a notebook, attach the script, and check the weeks with bonus points or team dances.]

blocks.text:
Of the 421 entries in the file, 128 are actors, 95 are athletes, 67 are TV personalities and 61 are singers or rappers. That is 351 of 421, about 83%. Models (17) and comedians (12) are the minor leagues.

Seasons ran between 6 and 16 contestants each.

blocks.title: What the file cannot tell you
blocks.text: Fan votes are not in it. Judge scores run 1 to 10, can be averages across several dances, and spread bonus points across judges. A score of 0 marks an eliminated contestant. And Judge 1 is not necessarily the same person from week to week, per COMAP's notes.
